topic: hospital funeral halls (jangnyesikjang): three-day funerals, all-night mourners, yukgaejang, wreaths, cremation
title: In Korea, Funerals Happen at the Hospital

slides.kicker: NOT AT HOME. NOT AT A CHURCH.
slides.headline: In Korea, funerals happen **at the hospital.**
slides.note: Three days, open doors, and a bowl of soup.

slides.headline: It's called a **jangnyesikjang**
slides.body: 장례식장, a funeral hall. Many big hospitals run one on a lower floor, with mourning rooms the family rents.

slides.headline: Once at home. **Then apartments.**
slides.body: Funerals used to be held in the family house. Apartments had no room for it, so from the 1990s hospitals took over.

slides.headline: Three days, **start to finish**
slides.body: It's called samiljang (삼일장). Day one, mourners arrive. Day two, the body is dressed. Day three, the procession leaves.

slides.headline: Mourners come **at any hour**
slides.body: No invitations needed. Friends and coworkers show up late at night, bow to the photo, then bow to the family.

slides.headline: Then **you eat**
slides.body: Every guest is fed: yukgaejang (육개장), a spicy beef soup, with rice and rice cakes. Nobody leaves hungry.

slides.headline: The hallway fills **with wreaths**
slides.body: Companies and friends send tall stands of white flowers with ribbons. The longer the row, the wider the circle.

slides.headline: Cremated **in 2024**
slides.body: Up from 33.5% in 2000. Graves on the hillside are giving way to urns.

slides.headline: Elsewhere a funeral home. **Here, a hospital.**
slides.body: In many countries the funeral home is its own business. In Korea, it is often the building next to the ward.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.

caption:
In Korea, most funerals happen at the hospital, in a funeral hall a few floors below the ward.

Three days, mourners at any hour, and every guest gets a bowl of soup.

Where does a funeral happen where you live?
reply: One more: many Korean families pay into a funeral plan for years before they ever need it. It's called sangjo (상조), and when the day comes it sends staff, a casket and mourning clothes. How do families prepare for a funeral where you live?
fact_check: 2장: 병원 장례식장 — 대형병원 지하·별관 장례식장, 빈소(분향실) 임대. 'many big hospitals'로 표기, 비율 단정 안 함.
3장: 1990년대 초 대형병원 전문 장례식장 등장 후 가정 장례가 병원·전문 장례식장으로 이동(주간경향). 아파트 공간 문제는 통설.
4장: 삼일장 — 1일 임종·빈소, 2일 염습·입관, 3일 발인. 일반적 순서.
5장: 조문 — 영정에 재배(또는 묵념), 상주와 맞절. 초대 없이 조문.
8장: 화장률 2000년 33.5% → 2024년 94.0%(보건복지부 2025, 보사연·한은 보고서 인용). 봉안·자연장 증가.
9장: 일반화 — 미국 등 독립 장의사(funeral home) 비교, 특정국 단정 안 함.
댓글: 상조 — 선불식 할부거래, 장례 인력·관·수의 제공.
